salmon.title: Lucy Maynard Salmon: social inquiry and historical teaching at Vassar
salmon.citation: Vassar Encyclopedia, “Lucy Maynard Salmon”; Salmon, Domestic Service (Macmillan, 1897).

verification.note: Vassar account checked for source criticism, everyday material evidence, and teaching. This early social inquiry is not assigned to the post-1950 new social history school. Rechecked complete institutional article on 2026-09-12: distinguishes source-critical pedagogy, later newspaper studies and institutional conflict. Its retrospective new-social-history language is not treated as membership; bibliography’s Domestic Service 1987 typo is not adopted. Named archival review folder is a lead, not a consulted review.

salmon_works.citation: Vassar Quarterly, “About Books” (2001), review of History and the Texture of Modern Life, including Salmon’s Domestic Service (1897).

verification.note: Institutional review identifies the 1897 study and her work with cookbooks and household material culture; retrospective support, not a contemporary influence record.

beard_force_primary.title: Mary Ritter Beard, Woman as Force in History: A Study in Traditions and Realities (Macmillan, 1946), preface.
beard_force_primary.citation: Mary Ritter Beard, Woman as Force in History: A Study in Traditions and Realities (Macmillan, 1946), preface.

verification.note: Complete preface, signed summer 1945, read in Andy Blunden’s transcription. It sets out the subject-sex argument, legal/equity inquiry, criticism of equality as a sufficient guide, and enlarged historical attention. Opening portions of chapters I and X also consulted, not complete chapters. Original printing and legal cases not collated. Transcription adds an article to the title; established bibliographic title retained. Beard’s generalizations are arguments, not independently verified facts.

beard_voss_archives.title: Anke Voss-Hubbard, “No Documents—No History”: Mary Ritter Beard and the Early History of Women’s Archives, American Archivist 58/1 (Winter 1995), pp. 16–30.
beard_voss_archives.citation: Anke Voss-Hubbard, “No Documents—No History”: Mary Ritter Beard and the Early History of Women’s Archives, American Archivist 58/1 (Winter 1995), pp. 16–30.

verification.note: Complete article read, including separately recovered pp. 21–22 and 26–27. Uses correspondence, annual reports and Grierson interviews to reconstruct WCWA and Smith collecting, cataloguing, teaching and donor work. Documents Black women’s marginal authority/funding and organizational disputes alongside achievements. Original letters/reports and Collier-Thomas’s cited 1986 essay are mediated, not independently read. No sole-founder claim or universal claim about women’s archives is adopted.

richter_spruill.title: Julie Richter, review of Julia Cherry Spruill, Women’s Life and Work in the Southern Colonies, H-SAWH, March 1999.
richter_spruill.citation: Julie Richter, review of Julia Cherry Spruill, Women’s Life and Work in the Southern Colonies, H-SAWH, March 1999.

verification.note: Complete review read from original H-Net HTML obtained with curl after browser access failed. Quotes Spruill’s original preface and p. 208, describes Scott’s reissue introduction, and documents Colonial Williamsburg use. Criticism concerns questions not asked about Black and Native women, not their total absence. Richter’s planned use for a slavery study is future intent. Book, original preface and Scott introductions remain mediated; friendship with Beard does not establish methodological transmission.

salmon_domestic_primary.title: Lucy Maynard Salmon, Domestic Service (1897; second edition, Macmillan, 1901), prefaces and chapters I–II.
salmon_domestic_primary.citation: Lucy Maynard Salmon, Domestic Service (1897; second edition, Macmillan, 1901), prefaces and chapters I–II.

verification.note: Title/copyright, complete original preface vii–xiv, second-edition preface xv and chapters I–II pp. 1–15 read in Gutenberg transcription. Documents survey distribution, nonresponse, bureau tabulation, named assistance and an economic/historical explanation. Second edition adds a European chapter; it is not attributed to 1897. The self-description as representative or random is not endorsed as modern probability sampling. Remaining chapters, original schedules and numerical calculations not audited; historical generalizations remain Salmon’s arguments.

salmon_progress_primary.title: Lucy Maynard Salmon, Progress in the Household (Houghton Mifflin, 1906), Apologia, pp. v–xiv.
salmon_progress_primary.citation: Lucy Maynard Salmon, Progress in the Household (Houghton Mifflin, 1906), Apologia, pp. v–xiv.

verification.note: Title/copyright and complete Apologia read. Salmon explains the investigation’s institutional origin, differentiates evidence from household panaceas, recalls disciplinary reception, and explicitly invokes Moses Coit Tyler’s instruction to assess a work by its purpose. Her conjectures about economists’ and historians’ reactions are not independently established reviews. Remaining essays unread.

flexner_james_review.title: Frances James, “Century of Women’s Struggle,” International Socialist Review 21/1 (Winter 1960), pp. 27–28.
flexner_james_review.citation: Frances James, “Century of Women’s Struggle,” International Socialist Review 21/1 (Winter 1960), pp. 27–28.

verification.note: Complete contemporary review read. Welcomes labor and Black women’s coverage but criticizes the absence of a private-property explanation and program beyond reform. These are James’s judgments. Quoted preface remains mediated; the review’s Sojourner Truth speech version is not treated as a verified transcript. Frances James is not conflated with Janet Wilson James.

flexner_ostrander_review.title: Gilman M. Ostrander, review of Century of Struggle, Ohio Historical Quarterly 70, pp. 90–91.
flexner_ostrander_review.citation: Gilman M. Ostrander, review of Century of Struggle, Ohio Historical Quarterly 70, pp. 90–91.

verification.note: Complete review read in Ohio History’s digitized volume. Praises extensive research but questions suffragist self-definition, causal integration of other reforms and treatment of temperance/evangelical support. Quotes Flexner’s narrower stated aim; this does not independently verify every book claim. Volume/pages checked; a publication year is not newly assigned without explicit issue metadata. Browser text accessible despite curl 403 responses.
